chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated that Abu Hashem Dawood ibn Al-Qasim al-Ja'fari narrated

He said: I used to eat lunch with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he would call some of his servants in Slavic and Persian. Sometimes I would send this servant of mine with something in Persian, and he (the Imam) would teach him. And sometimes the speech would become difficult/confusing for his servant in Persian, so he (the Imam) would clarify/explain it for his servant.
ai.seo_question: What languages did Imam al-Ridha (a.s.) speak and how did he interact with his servants?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith serves as a key evidence (hujjah) for the Imam’s comprehensive knowledge (‘ilm al-lugha), illustrating his practical mastery of Slavic and Persian to facilitate communication with diverse companions. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Imams’ linguistic versatility was not merely social but a divine attribute enabling them to convey religious guidance across cultural boundaries, reinforcing their role as accessible guides for the Ummah.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 54-2 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of Abu Hashem Dawood ibn Al-Qasim al-Ja’fari,

“I used to eat lunch with Abal Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.). Sometimes he (a.s.) spoke to some of his servants in Slavic and Persian (Farsi) languages. Sometimes I sent my servant who spoke Persian to the Imam (a.s.) and Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) knew Persian. Sometimes it became difficult for the servants to understand Persian. Then the Imam (a.s.) used to explain things for them himself.
